FINAL IVX ENTERPRISE STABILITY, TRAFFIC, TRANSACTION, AND CONNECTIVITY AUDIT
EXECUTE END TO END — FIX, TEST, DEPLOY, VERIFY

OBJECTIVE

Stabilize IVX Holdings as an enterprise production system before large public traffic, investor activity, online transactions, autonomous execution, and App Store / Google Play expansion.

Current confirmed incident classes include:

1. Portfolio rendering failures:
   - Cannot read property 'totalDeposited' of undefined
   - Cannot read property 'totalBalance' of undefined

2. Reels instability:
   - Reels crashes after several minutes of use

3. IVX IA Chat timeout:
   - BACKEND_POST_STARTED succeeded
   - BACKEND_POST_FINISHED timed out after 90,000 ms
   - no HTTP response received

These bugs may affect user traffic, online connectivity, transaction confidence, API reliability, autonomous work, mobile stability, and production trust.

Do not fix only the visible screen.
Audit the entire enterprise request, data, transaction, traffic, and recovery architecture.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — OPEN ENTERPRISE INCIDENT
==================================================

Create one production incident covering:

- Portfolio crash
- Wallet and balance rendering
- Reels long-session crash
- Chat backend timeout
- API reliability
- transaction safety
- traffic readiness
- connected-service stability

Assign:

Severity: SEV-1 if financial or transaction data is affected
Severity: SEV-2 if limited to screen availability with no financial loss

Record:

- incident ID
- first observed time
- affected build
- affected devices
- affected routes
- trace IDs
- APIs involved
- production commit
- deployment ID
- owner
- current status

Do not close the incident until production verification is complete.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — COMPLETE SYSTEM DEPENDENCY MAP
==================================================

Map the complete IVX production flow:

Mobile / Web
→ Authentication
→ API Gateway
→ Backend Routes
→ Business Services
→ Supabase
→ Storage
→ Realtime
→ Worker Queue
→ Autonomous Workers
→ GitHub
→ Render
→ AWS
→ EAS
→ Notifications
→ Payments / Transactions
→ Executive Layer

For every connection identify:

- endpoint
- protocol
- authentication
- timeout
- retry policy
- idempotency
- rate limit
- database dependency
- external provider
- failure behavior
- monitoring
- recovery method

Mark every connection:

VERIFIED
PARTIAL
UNVERIFIED
FAILED

==================================================
PHASE 3 — PORTFOLIO AND WALLET ROOT-CAUSE AUDIT
==================================================

Search the complete codebase for:

- totalDeposited
- totalBalance
- availableBalance
- portfolioValue
- walletBalance
- holdings
- deposits
- withdrawals
- transactions

For every property access identify:

- exact file
- exact line
- parent object
- TypeScript type
- API source
- initialization state
- loading state
- empty state
- error state
- authorization condition

Determine why the parent object becomes undefined.

Possible causes to prove or reject:

- API returned missing object
- request not completed
- session expired
- 401/403 response
- backend error
- incorrect field mapping
- race condition
- stale cache
- first-render timing
- incomplete account record
- failed Supabase query
- inconsistent mobile and backend types

Do not resolve this only with optional chaining.

Required correction:

- canonical backend response contract
- runtime schema validation
- typed client model
- safe initial state
- verified empty-state handling
- explicit unauthorized state
- explicit failed state
- bounded retry
- no state update after unmount
- traceable error logs

==================================================
PHASE 4 — FINANCIAL DATA INTEGRITY
==================================================

Audit all financial values shown in Portfolio, Wallet, Investor, Capital Pipeline, and Executive Layer.

Verify:

- total balance
- available balance
- total deposited
- total withdrawn
- capital committed
- capital received
- capital deployed
- profits
- distributions
- escrow
- transaction history
- portfolio value
- ROI
- cash runway

Every value must trace to:

- database table
- row ID
- transaction ID
- ledger entry
- timestamp
- calculation
- API response

Never convert an unavailable financial source to $0 unless the account is verified as genuinely empty.

Use these states:

VERIFIED_ZERO
VERIFIED_VALUE
LOADING
UNAVAILABLE
FAILED
UNAUTHORIZED

No fake charts.
No decorative financial growth.
No estimated balances presented as real.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — TRANSACTION SAFETY AUDIT
==================================================

Audit every money-related workflow:

- investor commitment
- deposit
- withdrawal
- wallet transfer
- subscription
- escrow transfer
- capital allocation
- capital deployment
- profit distribution
- refund
- payment confirmation
- bank reconciliation

For every transaction verify:

1. Unique transaction ID
2. Idempotency key
3. Server-side validation
4. Authentication
5. Authorization
6. Available-balance validation
7. Atomic database operation
8. Double-entry or auditable ledger
9. Provider response storage
10. Retry protection
11. Duplicate prevention
12. Webhook verification
13. Final settlement status
14. Audit log
15. Reconciliation process

Required statuses:

CREATED
PENDING
AUTHORIZED
PROCESSING
SETTLED
FAILED
REVERSED
REFUNDED
CANCELLED

Never mark a transaction complete from the mobile client alone.

Never allow repeated taps or network retries to create duplicate financial operations.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — IDEMPOTENCY AND DUPLICATE PREVENTION
==================================================

Implement idempotency across:

- financial transactions
- autonomous jobs
- chat messages
- investor commitments
- document signing
- notifications
- webhook processing
- deployment requests

Use:

- owner ID
- user ID
- conversation ID
- message ID
- transaction ID
- request hash
- provider event ID

A repeated request must return the existing result instead of creating a duplicate.

Add database uniqueness constraints where appropriate.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — CHAT TIMEOUT AND ASYNC JOB FIX
==================================================

Current failure:

POST begins
→ backend waits for long-running work
→ no response for 90 seconds
→ mobile marks request blocked

Correct architecture:

Chat request
→ backend validates
→ persistent job created
→ HTTP 202 returned in under 5 seconds
→ worker executes asynchronously
→ mobile polls or subscribes
→ progress events appear
→ final result appears

Required:

POST /api/ivx/senior-developer/worker/jobs

Return:

{
  "taskId": "...",
  "status": "QUEUED",
  "statusUrl": "...",
  "createdAt": "..."
}

Implement:

- job persistence
- heartbeat
- status polling
- reconnect
- resume after restart
- retry without duplication
- stale-job recovery
- terminal states
- owner cancellation
- owner approval gates

Do not solve this by only increasing the timeout.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — REELS LONG-SESSION STABILITY
==================================================

Run a forensic Reels test for at least 60 minutes.

Test:

- 200+ reel transitions
- continuous autoplay
- pause and resume
- background and foreground
- network loss and recovery
- Wi-Fi to cellular
- repeated tab changes
- repeated open and close
- mixed image and video media
- comments
- likes
- sharing
- uploads
- low-memory conditions

Measure:

- memory
- CPU
- active video players
- active listeners
- active subscriptions
- timers
- cached media
- network calls
- duplicate records
- dropped frames
- crash stack

Correct:

- player disposal
- listener cleanup
- subscription cleanup
- timer cleanup
- stable list keys
- bounded preload
- bounded cache
- pagination deduplication
- one active player
- unmount safety
- background pause
- failed-media retry limits

==================================================
PHASE 9 — API RELIABILITY
==================================================

Audit every production API.

For each endpoint test:

- valid request
- empty response
- malformed response
- unauthorized
- forbidden
- not found
- server error
- database timeout
- network timeout
- slow response
- repeated request
- concurrent request
- partial dependency failure

Required:

- documented timeout
- retry policy
- circuit breaker where appropriate
- structured error response
- trace ID
- request ID
- sanitized logs
- rate limit
- health metric
- latency metric

No request may hang indefinitely.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — TRAFFIC AND CAPACITY TESTING
==================================================

Run controlled load tests in stages:

Stage 1:
10 concurrent users

Stage 2:
100 concurrent users

Stage 3:
1,000 concurrent users

Stage 4:
10,000 simulated users only after lower stages pass

Test separately:

- login
- registration
- landing page
- members
- investors
- portfolio
- transactions
- reels
- chat
- autonomous jobs
- notifications
- Executive Layer

Measure:

- requests per second
- p50 latency
- p90 latency
- p95 latency
- p99 latency
- error rate
- timeout rate
- CPU
- memory
- database connections
- queue depth
- worker utilization

Do not claim support for 100M users based on small synthetic tests.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — DATABASE ENTERPRISE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

- indexes
- slow queries
- connection pooling
- RLS
- migrations
- foreign keys
- unique constraints
- transaction isolation
- locks
- deadlocks
- backups
- point-in-time recovery
- replication
- retention
- audit logs

Verify critical financial writes use atomic database transactions.

Verify no client can modify protected balances directly.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — AUTHENTICATION AND AUTHORIZATION
==================================================

Test:

- owner login
- investor login
- buyer login
- member login
- admin access
- session refresh
- expired token
- revoked token
- logout
- app restart
- invalid password
- non-owner rejection
- role escalation attempts

Every privileged route must enforce authorization on the server.

Do not rely only on hidden mobile buttons.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — CONNECTED SERVICES
==================================================

Verify all external and internal integrations:

- Supabase
- Render
- GitHub
- AWS
- EAS
- email
- SMS
- notifications
- payment provider
- bank or escrow provider
- analytics
- error monitoring

For each service record:

- status
- credential binding
- last successful request
- failure response
- timeout
- retry
- fallback
- alerting

Only request new credentials if runtime proves missing, revoked, expired, 401, or 403.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — OBSERVABILITY
==================================================

Implement or verify:

- mobile crash reporting
- backend error monitoring
- distributed trace IDs
- API latency dashboards
- database monitoring
- queue monitoring
- worker heartbeat dashboard
- transaction reconciliation alerts
- failed-login alerts
- deployment monitoring
- release health

Every production error must answer:

- who was affected
- which build
- which route
- which API
- which commit
- which deployment
- which trace ID
- whether money or data was affected

==================================================
PHASE 15 — RELEASE SAFETY
==================================================

All future improvements must use:

Feature Branch
→ Automated Tests
→ Code Review
→ Staging
→ Physical Device QA
→ Release Candidate
→ Canary Release
→ Production Monitoring
→ Full Rollout

Required controls:

- feature flags
- staged rollout
- rollback
- database migration rollback plan
- compatible Expo runtime
- no incompatible OTA update
- previous stable build retained
- automatic rollback on critical crash increase

==================================================
PHASE 16 — AUTOMATED REGRESSION
==================================================

Create permanent tests for:

Portfolio:
- missing object
- null values
- empty account
- populated account
- expired session
- timeout
- retry
- remount
- app restart

Transactions:
- duplicate tap
- repeated request
- network interruption
- provider retry
- webhook replay
- insufficient balance
- partial failure
- settlement reconciliation

Reels:
- 200-item scroll
- 60-minute playback
- background/foreground
- memory stability
- cleanup
- pagination

Chat:
- 202 response
- job creation
- status polling
- reconnect
- restart persistence
- duplicate prevention
- worker timeout

Run:

- lint
- typecheck
- unit tests
- integration tests
- contract tests
- API tests
- security tests
- mobile smoke tests
- transaction tests
- load tests

==================================================
PHASE 17 — DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

After all release-blocking failures are fixed:

1. Commit changes.
2. Push to owner-controlled GitHub.
3. Run CI.
4. Deploy staging.
5. Complete physical-device QA.
6. Create release candidate.
7. Deploy backend.
8. Publish compatible mobile build/update.
9. Verify Android.
10. Verify iOS.
11. Verify web.
12. Verify transactions.
13. Verify Reels for 60 minutes.
14. Verify Chat async execution.
15. Verify production monitoring.
16. Keep rollback immediately available.

==================================================
PHASE 18 — REQUIRED EVIDENCE
==================================================

Return:

INCIDENT
- incident ID
- severity
- affected systems
- confirmed root causes

PORTFOLIO
- file
- line
- data source
- contract fix
- test evidence

REELS
- crash stack
- memory evidence
- lifecycle fix
- sustained test duration

CHAT
- request duration before
- request duration after
- HTTP 202 proof
- task ID
- polling evidence
- heartbeat evidence

TRANSACTIONS
- idempotency evidence
- ledger evidence
- reconciliation test
- duplicate prevention test

TRAFFIC
- concurrency levels
- latency
- error rate
- resource usage
- passed capacity

PRODUCTION
- repository
- branch
- commit SHA
- Render deployment ID
- EAS build/update ID
- APK/AAB version
- iOS build version
- /health HTTP 200
- GitHub HEAD
- live commit
- commit match
- verification timestamps

==================================================
FINAL RELEASE GATES
==================================================

Do not mark PRODUCTION READY until:

[ ] Portfolio never crashes on missing data.
[ ] Financial values are verified and traceable.
[ ] Transactions are atomic and idempotent.
[ ] Duplicate requests cannot duplicate money movements.
[ ] Reels passes 60 minutes and 200+ transitions.
[ ] Chat returns HTTP 202 and runs asynchronously.
[ ] APIs pass reliability and timeout tests.
[ ] Authentication and authorization pass.
[ ] Traffic tests pass at the approved level.
[ ] Database backup and recovery are verified.
[ ] Monitoring and alerts are live.
[ ] Android passes.
[ ] iOS passes.
[ ] Web passes.
[ ] Rollback is tested.
[ ] GitHub HEAD equals the live production commit.
[ ] No critical or high-severity incident remains open.

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE FORMAT
==================================================

OVERALL STATUS:
PASS / FAIL

PORTFOLIO:
VERIFIED / FAILED

REELS:
VERIFIED / FAILED

CHAT:
VERIFIED / FAILED

TRANSACTIONS:
VERIFIED / FAILED / NOT IMPLEMENTED

TRAFFIC CAPACITY:
VERIFIED LEVEL: ___ concurrent users

ANDROID:
VERIFIED / FAILED

IOS:
VERIFIED / FAILED / NOT TESTED

WEB:
VERIFIED / FAILED

PRODUCTION:
DEPLOYED / NOT DEPLOYED

OPEN BLOCKERS:
List every remaining blocker with exact evidence.

Do not return a narrative completion report.
Return only reproducible technical and production evidence.
